keyVerseText: This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, according to the number of your persons; take ye every man for them which are in his tents. for every: Heb. by the poll, or, head persons: Heb. souls
rootMeaning: The Hebrew root of עֹמֶר (ʻômer) is עָמַר (ʻâmar), which fundamentally means to bind sheaves or to gather grain. This root conveys the action of collecting and bundling harvested crops, emphasizing the physical act of gathering and preparing grain. Beyond the common English term 'sheaf,' the root sense enriches the word by highlighting the process and care involved in harvesting and handling food, reflecting both agricultural practice and provision.
usageInScripture: The term עֹמֶר appears 14 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently referring either to a 'sheaf' of grain or to a specific dry measure approximately one-tenth of an ephah (about 2 liters). The top translations show it most frequently as 'the sheaf' or 'an omer,' indicating both a physical bundle of grain and a standardized measure for food. This dual usage reveals the word's practical role in the economy and worship life of ancient Israel, linking sustenance with ritual significance.
theologicalSignificance: The word עֹמֶר carries deep theological weight as it connects God's provision with human responsibility in gathering and measuring sustenance. It reminds believers that God commands orderly stewardship of His gifts, as seen in the prescribed measure of the omer. This term also points forward to Christ as the bread of life, the true provision gathered and offered for His people. Understanding עֹמֶר enriches our appreciation of God's care in both physical nourishment and spiritual sustenance, underscoring His faithfulness and the call to trust in His provision.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 16:16 states, 'This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, according to the number of your persons.' Here, the word עֹמֶר defines the precise quantity each person is to gather, emphasizing God's provision tailored to individual needs. The term's meaning as a dry measure highlights God's orderly provision in the wilderness, teaching reliance on Him daily. This measure symbolizes God's faithfulness to supply exactly what is needed, no more and no less, fostering dependence on His grace.
